chapter: The band, its players and singers
title: What Freddie Green gives the band
summary: Basie says Freddie Green gives the band a sound and fullness, ties up loose ends, and is the only unamplified guitarist who can be heard.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: How about Freddie?
What do you mean? What about him?
Freddie Green.
What about him?
What does he give to the band?
Freddie gives the band a sound which --
What sound?
Sound, and he keeps things together.
Does he?

He gives a little fullness and everything, you know, you can always use some chords and sound going along there. He sort of tights up the loose ends there and when he's not there, we certainly miss him. He's the only guy I know that plays a guitar that's not amplified and you hear him.
How do you hear him as separate from the bass?
What do you mean how do I hear him separate from the bass? What kind of questions are these? How do I hear him? I just hear him.
What does he do different? How does he tie things together differently from, say, the bass tying things together. The bass doesn't tie things together, the bass --
He fits in, (inaudible) bottom line.
He's the bottom line.
How do you think he fits in? You got answers for all these questions.
I never quite understood -- I tried to understand how the bass, and the guitar go. I don't know.
Try, you might give me some points -- it might be a big help.
Yeah.
Yeah, I'm not kidding.
Well, I'll think about it.
